title: Riemann Hypothesis over the Holographic Substrate

rows.label: A3

blocks.title: The de-framing dictionary and the completeness criterion

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The dictionary [chart]: horizon $\sqrt \p\leftrightarrow$ Riemann--Siegel length $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$, half-turn $\leftrightarrow n^{-1/2}$, scale $\leftrightarrow\log n$; a shell of cardinality $\p$ reads $\zeta$ on the line to $T=2\pi \p$, one cycle of the shell, and a height is the scale coordinate of the shell that reads it, its count using residues below $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$ only.

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: Zero density is shell scale-depth: at $T=2\pi \p$ the smooth Riemann--von Mangoldt density is $\frac1{2\pi}\log \p$, $0.6226,0.9891,1.3556,1.7220$ at $\p=50,500,5\cdot10^{3},5\cdot10^{4}$ [chart]; a substitution under the dictionary, recorded as a consistency, not a test.

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: Reconstruction residue: the finite-horizon error of the main sum is the Riemann--Siegel remainder $O(T^{-1/4})=O(\p^{-1/4})$ (A6), unconditional, fitted slope $-0.24$ over $t=40\ldots5120$ [approx].

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: The bare horizon-length sum locates the first zeros: one sign change per zero of $\zeta$ on $[10,55]$, each within $0.5$ of $\gamma_n$, from one or two terms [approx].

rows.label: D5
rows.predicate: The cells: the heights of a Carrier's cycle are its residues, residue $y$ the cell from $2\pi y$ to $2\pi(y+1)$; a cell is clean when its zeros lie on the line, which Turing's count decides from the labels below $\sqrt{y+1}$, and passes when the frame's reading certifies it. The hypothesis of the Carrier: every residue has a clean cell.

rows.label: D6
rows.predicate: The finite readings are approximations: at any depth neither reading produces an exact zero, neither uses nor supplies the hypothesis; completeness is stated in the zero-mode basis, and no transfer from the units-chart order of C3 is asserted or used.

rows.label: D7
rows.predicate: The reconstruction is on-line: $Z(T)$ is real on the line, so every point it produces has $\Real=\half$, a property of the reading; the hypothesis is then the completeness clause of D5, the faithfulness of the de-framing, and likewise for each $\chi$-twist (E14).

rows.label: D8
rows.predicate: The strip: the Euler product excludes zeros with real part at least one, and the functional equation confines the nontrivial zeros to the open strip in Klein-four orbits of size two on the line and four off it; the Davenport--Heilbronn vector, without the product, is not multiplicative and has an off-line zero. No core witness: the statement is analytic.

rows.label: D9

blocks.title: The scale-evolution spectrum from the prime side, and the shell theorem

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The scale-evolution generator: on the shell the scale-shift $x\mapsto\gen^{\,r}x$ is a unitary permutation of $\Fx{\p}$ with the complex characters as eigenvectors; in the analytic chart [chart] the dilation group $U_r=e^{ir\Hh}$ has the self-adjoint generator $\Hh=-i(x\partial_x+\half)$ with generalised eigenfunctions $x^{-\bar\rho}$, $\rho=\half+i\gamma$, the symmetrizing $\half$ the half-turn of B8; the chart assignment is used nowhere as a shell identity.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: The Hilbert--P\'olya target correspondence: the de-framing on the spectrum is $\rho\mapsto-i(\rho-\half)$, real on the nontrivial zeros iff the hypothesis; $\sigma(\Hh)=\{-i(\rho-\half)\}$ is the target, not a result. The exhibited operator is the Jacobi matrix $\mathbf J_N$ (E9), a realisation every finite real multiset admits; its identification with a discretisation of $\Hh$ is not asserted and used by no row.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: Cutoff and semiclassical density: with the space quantum $1_\Omega$ as lower cutoff the Berry--Keating phase-space count is the Riemann--von Mangoldt count, density the shell scale-depth of D2 [chart]; the cell normalisation $1_\Omega^{2}\sim2\pi$ is imposed [chart] (A11).

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: Prime--zero duality on the scale axis: $\sum\Lambda(n)n^{-s}=-\zeta'/\zeta$, poles at $s=1$, the nontrivial zeros and the trivial zeros; the poles on the self-dual axis are exactly the on-line zeros, an off-line zero a pole at its own location off the axis.

rows.label: E5
rows.predicate: The heights from the primes, $\zeta$ never evaluated: the tapered scale-spectrum $\Sigma_N(\gamma)$ of the comb to $N=10^{6}$ peaks at the first six heights within $0.03$, each peak several times the baseline, width $\sim2\pi/\log N$ [approx].

rows.label: E6
rows.predicate: The discrete eigenvalues from the comb: the raw count $\widetilde{\mathcal N}_N(T)=\theta(T)/\pi+1+S_{\mathrm{comb}}(T)$ carries the pole term (F8) and has no limit in $N$; the pole-corrected count $\widehat{\mathcal N}_N=\widetilde{\mathcal N}_N-\tfrac1\pi\Im[\Pi_N+\log\tfrac{s-1}{s}]$ crosses $n-\half$ near the zeros, its secular condition recovering the first ten heights to mean error $3.4\times10^{-5}$ at $N=10^{6}$ and $1.3\times10^{-5}$ at $10^{8}$; the raw condition stalls past $10^{7}$ [approx].

rows.label: E7
rows.predicate: The limits are finitist refinements: $N\to\infty$ is a sequence of finite reframings, the comb depth the refinement depth, no completed infinity invoked; a comb of depth $N$ is the window of a Subject with $\sqrt \p\ge N$ (B3), so the exhibited combs are read on $\p\ge N^{2}$, embedded while $\Omega\gg N^{4}$; each construction's (heights, main-sum length, depth, Subject) is recorded.

rows.label: E8
rows.predicate: The heights from an explicit matrix: the colleague matrix of the Chebyshev expansion of $\cos(\pi\widehat{\mathcal N}_N)$ on $[10,52]$ at $N=10^{6}$ returns the ten heights to mean error $4.8\times10^{-5}$ at dimension $520$ and $3.5\times10^{-5}$ at $620$, converging to the corrected roots' own $3.4\times10^{-5}$ at this depth [approx]; the precision is the smoothed count's, not the comb's (A9).

rows.label: E9
rows.predicate: The comb-built Jacobi realisation: the real-symmetric tridiagonal matrix of the height measure of the corrected secular roots has those roots as its exact spectrum ($4\times10^{-14}$ [approx]) and the heights to $3.4\times10^{-5}$, with the stated ten coefficients $a$, $b$; self-adjointness is free (every finite real multiset is such a spectrum), so it imposes no constraint.

rows.label: E10
rows.predicate: Additive injection is gauge-trivial: $-i\,d/du+V$ is unitarily equivalent to $-i\,d/du$ with a shifted boundary phase, its spectrum uniform; numerically the spacing standard deviation of $-i\,d/du+V_{\mathrm{comb}}$ is $0.11$ of its mean against the heights' $0.39$ [approx]; the comb enters through the trace.

rows.label: E11
rows.predicate: GUE level repulsion of the target spectrum: unfolded spacings of the first $240$ zeros give $P(s<\half)=0.05$ (GUE $\approx0.12$, Poisson $\approx0.39$) and variance $0.13$ (GUE $\approx0.18$, Poisson $1$) [approx]; a known statistic (A9) reproduced.

rows.label: E12
rows.predicate: \textbf{The shell theorem.} On every shell, with no hypothesis: (i) $v$ expands in the constant mode and the nonterminal modes of the quarter-turn meridian; (ii) every readout lies on $\Tr=1$, real part $2^{-1}=2\kp+1=-\pi$; (iii) the scale-shift has the modes as eigenvectors, eigenphases $2\pi j/(\p-1)$ independent of $v$. No off-line mode; true of every vector, the Davenport--Heilbronn vector included.

rows.predicate: Shell-basis completeness is not a clause of E12: the $\p-1$ complex characters are an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb C^{\Fx{\p}}$ ($\lVert\chi_j\rVert^{2}=\p-1$; finite Parseval), true of every vector, the trivial character carrying the mean $\psi(\p-1)/(\p-1)$; the $\Fp$-valued power characters are never orthonormal and do not expand $v$; completeness for the zero set of $\zeta$ is D5, a different clause.

rows.label: E14
rows.predicate: The $\chi$-twist: for a real character the twisted vector is self-conjugate, the twisted secular condition recovering six heights of $L(s,\chi_{-4})$ to mean error $8.6\times10^{-5}$ [approx]; for a primitive complex character the root number's half-phase and the matching $\Gamma$-factor restore the self-dual structure (E16); the generalized hypothesis is read as the twisted de-framing's faithfulness, as D5.

rows.label: E15
rows.predicate: Twisted-comb validation, $\chi_{-4}$: $\widetilde{\mathcal N}_{N,\chi}=\theta_\chi/\pi+S^{\chi}_{\mathrm{comb}}$, with no pole term to remove, reads $0.4997,\dots,5.4998$ at the first six zeros of $L(s,\chi)$ (located via Hurwitz zeta), and the twisted secular condition with the $N=10^{6}$ comb recovers $6.0209,\dots,21.4506$ to mean error $8.6\times10^{-5}$, $L$ never evaluated [approx].

rows.label: E16
rows.predicate: Twisted-comb validation, the complex character of conductor $5$ ($\chi(2)=i$, odd): the half-phase $W(\chi)^{-1/2}\Lambda(\half+it,\chi)$ is real on the line to $10^{-20}$; the twisted count rounds to the exact integers $1,\dots,14$ midway between the fifteen zeros below $40$, within $3\times10^{-4}$; the twisted secular condition with the $N=10^{6}$ comb, $L$ never evaluated, recovers the fifteen heights to mean error $8.0\times10^{-5}$ [approx].

blocks.title: The screen reading: the value and its control

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: \textbf{Turing's count on the shell.} On every cell $C_y\le N^{\mathrm{crit}}_y\le\mathcal N_y$ (A7); the cell is clean when $\mathcal N_y=N^{\mathrm{crit}}_y$, and $C_y=\mathcal N_y$ certifies it with every zero simple. The shell estimates $\mathcal N$ by the pole-corrected comb count (F8; uncertified at finite depth) and $C$ by the main sum's sign changes (A10). An off-line zero is a phantom: $\mathcal N_y-N^{\mathrm{crit}}_y>0$.

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: \textbf{The screen reading.} By D5 and F1 the classical hypothesis below $T$ is the value $\mathcal N(T)-N_{\mathrm{crit}}(T)=0$, both terms estimated on the shell, the count from the pole-corrected comb (convergent under the hypothesis, uncertified at finite depth), the on-line zeros from the sign changes (exact where certified, A10, and simple). Declared, not derived; E12 uses no Euler product.

rows.label: F3
rows.predicate: The control on the line: the completed Davenport--Heilbronn $\Lambda_f$ is real on the line to $10^{-20}$ [approx]; on $[0,87]$ the argument principle counts $N_f=45$ strip zeros against $C=43$ sign changes, the deficit $2$ opening only in the band of the off-line pair (A8), where $|Z_f|$ dips to $0.357$ without crossing; the constituent $L(s,\chi)$ closes with deficit $0$.

rows.label: F4
rows.predicate: The negative control on the comb side: the secular condition on the generalized comb $\Lambda_f$ (divisor recursion from the coefficients) returns two ``on-line'' roots at the phantom height, $85.65/85.75$ (comb to $4\times10^{5}$), where the line holds no zero; the raw count near the pair drifts with depth, $45.14\to45.73$ at $t=85.9$, and is stable away from it [approx].

rows.label: F5
rows.predicate: The $\zeta$ comb at its own singularity, the pole: at $t=1$ (exact count $0$) the raw count drifts, $+0.09\ldots-1.46$ over depths $10^{4}\ldots8\times10^{7}$, while at $t=15$ it stays within $2\times10^{-3}$ of $1$; the pole-corrected count at $t=1$ falls monotonically, $0.0051\to0.0012$ [approx]. The drift is the pole term of F8: no rounding bound for the raw count is depth-independent (F1).

rows.label: F6
rows.predicate: The Euler-product reading: an Euler product is the signature of a single multiplicative structure; the Davenport--Heilbronn function, a superposition of two, has the self-dual line and the functional symmetry and lacks the product; the screen reading separates the cases by the value $\mathcal N-N_{\mathrm{crit}}$ and places no zero on the line by fiat.

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: \textbf{The closure of the heights.} A height is a residue on the cycle of the shell that reads it, the largest shell is the Carrier's and there is no height beyond its cycle (A2); no embedded Subject reads the cycle whole (A4). The hypothesis of the Carrier is a statement about the residues of its cycle, one clause per residue.

rows.label: F8
rows.predicate: \textbf{The smoothed explicit formula.} Under the hypothesis of no zero to the right of the line, $\sum_{n\le N}\Lambda(n)w(n)n^{-s}/\log n=\Pi_N(s)+J_N(s)$ exactly, $\Pi_N$ explicit and growing with $N$, $J_N(s)\to G(s)=\log((s-1)\zeta(s)/s)$ off the zeros: the pole-corrected count converges to $\mathcal N(T)$. An off-line zero adds an explicit term $-\Pi^{(\rho)}_N$ (Rem.~\ref{rem:combsettle}); a collection of such zeros growing with the depth is not summed. Observed: the corrected counts settle (D2f, D2g, D3) [approx].

blocks.title: Horizon: the values beyond the embedded reader

rows.label: Z1
rows.predicate: The uniform value $\mathcal N=N_{\mathrm{crit}}$ over the Carrier's cycle, and the value at each height in $(2\pi\sqrt\Omega,\,2\pi\Omega]$: read by the shell whose scale is that height, no embedded Subject; the failing computation is the count at that height from any embedded window. Whether a finite-description proof exists is a question no row poses; positivity (\S\ref{sec:promotion}) is not attempted.

rows.label: Z2
rows.predicate: The heights as Carrier residues: under the frame-covariance of the height chart (A1) each $\gamma$ is a residue on the frequency latitude $L_{\kp+1}$ of the Carrier, its exact index below the resolution of every embedded Subject; finite-precision readings remain available to every Subject for the heights its scale reaches.

rows.label: Z5
rows.predicate: The uniform flatness bound over the shells: with $M(\p)=\max_{j\ne0}\lvert\langle\mathbf1_\Pi,\chi_j\rangle\rvert/(\lVert\mathbf1_\Pi-\bar{\mathbf1}_\Pi\rVert\,\lVert\chi_j\rVert)$ the normalised correlation of the shell's prime indicator with the chart modes, mean removed (floor $1/\sqrt{\p-2}$, C5), the bound $M(\p)=O(\p^{-1/2}\log^{5/2}\p)$; the generalized hypothesis modulo $\p$ implies it [import: \citealp[Ch.~20]{davenport2000}], the converse not asserted. Each shell's maximum is a finite computation (C6), the uniform bound read by no embedded Subject.

legend.name: Import
legend.text: A standard result, a corpus result, or a measured datum used here without reproof.

legend.name: Definition
legend.text: A naming, a declared dictionary, or a set-up move, carrying no empirical content.

legend.name: Theorem
legend.text: Derived within this paper from the rows above it, or an exact instance check in integer arithmetic; a predicate whose content is a numerical observation carries its figures as declared [approx]/[chart] and is a theorem in the weaker sense that the linked witness reproduces them to the stated tolerance on the tested instances --- the closing paragraph lists the two grades separately.

legend.name: $\Omega$-hard
legend.text: A value decided by the totality, in no embedded reader's window; a demarcation of where the value is read, not an open item.

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.registered_finite
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — the registered Universe is finite: whatever the totality `U`, what a reading of capacity `R` registers of it embeds in the shell of `R` members. No finiteness of `U` is assumed; the bound is the reading's, a record being finite (29:C1).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.no_unlimited_supply
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — no reading registers an unlimited supply: among any `R + 1` members of the totality, a reading of capacity `R` gives two the same residue, found by search (the pigeonhole `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`, 5:C2; the idleness of the unbounded supply, 29:C2).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.agent_bound
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — the agent's bound, the row's instance at capacity `R = records s K` (29:C1): a shell read whole — injectively — into the records of an agent of capacity `K` over `s ≥ 2` symbols has at most `records s K` members, fewer than `s^(K+1)` (`complete_needs_whole` at `o = records s K`, `records_lt`; 5:C2). The row's finitude clauses are `registered_finite` and `no_unlimited_supply` above; the structural cardinality Ω is A7's, consumed.

A3.name: FRC.Foundation.registration_onto
A3.doc: 20:A3, A3 — whatever exists is registered within: the registration of any totality is onto its registered Universe (the definition of `Registered` read back: every residue has a member). The row's "no outside, no host" is A8's and A1's, consumed by reference, not this theorem's: the conjunct holds on a shell read inside a larger host.

A3.name: FRC.Foundation.mutual_registration_count
A3.doc: 20:A3, A3 — two totalities each registered whole within the other have one count: injections both ways between shells force `m = n` (the pigeonhole `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`, 5:C2, both ways). With A6, one count is one Carrier. Silent on a host: a shell with more points registers a shell with fewer.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.observer_part
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, first clause) — a bounded observer is a proper part: an observer with `o < Ω` states holds no injective encoding of the Carrier's `Ω` points, and every reading `ρ` into its states identifies two distinct points (the pigeonhole, `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`; 25:D1, 5:C2). The two points are found by search.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.complete_needs_whole
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, second clause) — a complete reading needs the whole count: a reading of the `Ω` points into `o` records that identifies no two points has `Ω ≤ o` (the contrapositive of `observer_part`). A reader that is not the whole reads incompletely.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.translation_torsor
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, third clause) — the Carrier is a translation torsor (A6): exactly one translation carries each member to each. The origin is frame data: the shell's `0` is the chart's, and the translation carrying `0` to `x` makes `x` an origin as good; the affine frames are a torsor under the frame group (1:C2, `simply_transitive`).

D5.name: FRC.Horizon.clean_iff_count
D5.doc: 20:D5, the cells: a finite list of points with an involution (the reflection `s ↦ 1 − s̄`, say) has every point fixed exactly when the count of fixed points equals the count.

D5.name: FRC.Horizon.cells_clean_iff_cycle

D9.name: FRC.Horizon.negative_control13
D9.doc: 20:D9, the finite negative control: on `𝔽₁₃(√2)` (`η² = 2`, `2` a nonsquare, `2⁻¹ = 7`) the polynomial `P(X) = ((X − 2)² − 2)((X + 1)² − 2)` has exactly the four roots `2 ± η`, `−1 ± η`, of traces `4, 4, 11, 11` against the trace-one line's `1` (`Tr z = 1 ⟺ Re z = 7`), its root set closed under conjugation and under the half-turn `X ↦ 1 − X`: finitude, conjugation and the functional-equation reflection do not force roots onto the line. Decided by the kernel on all `169` elements.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.closure
F7.doc: 20:F7, the foundation clauses of Theorem closure. (i) The wrap of the height reading: a height `T + p` reads as the residue `T` on the cycle of the shell of cardinality `p`, and the successor reaches every residue of the cycle from `0` within `p` steps (00:A5, `successor_cycle`). (ii) Finitude: a reading of capacity `Ω` embeds the registered heights in the shell of `Ω` members (00:A2, `registered_finite`). (iii) Observation: a reading of `o < Ω` states identifies two residues of the Carrier's cycle, and a reading that identifies none has `Ω ≤ o` (00:A4, `observer_part`, `complete_needs_whole`). No axioms.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.closure_lab
F7.doc: 20:F7, the laboratory instances: for each laboratory Carrier `Ω = 13, 233, 30089, 2408561` (prime, `≡ 1 mod 4`) the largest embedded Subject `p* = 3, 13, 173, 1549` with `p*² < Ω < p'²`, `p'` the next prime (no prime between), so every embedded Subject's cycle is shorter than the Carrier's and the Carrier's top cell is read from labels up to `√Ω`, beyond every embedded window `√p*`. Primality by trial division to the root (`isPrime_of_bounded`), decided by the kernel.
